subject.title: refactor: separate external conversations from local sessions

question: Should OpenClaw adopt these conversation tools, Gateway methods, and durable per-agent delivery records as the permanent core contract for exact external addressing?
rationale: This establishes a new model-facing API, Gateway protocol surface, plugin retry contract, and persisted state model; automated tests cannot determine whether that breadth is the intended long-term product boundary.

options.title: Adopt the core contract
options.body: Accept the architecture after live Reef, upgrade, restart-recovery, and public plugin-contract evidence are attached.

options.title: Narrow to a generic seam
options.body: Keep conversation identity and correlation generic but defer some model-facing tools or durable operation storage until a smaller contract is agreed.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Continue using explicit message-tool targets and established session behavior while gathering more cross-channel design evidence.

recommendation.title: Adopt the core contract
recommendation.body: Accept the architecture after live Reef, upgrade, restart-recovery, and public plugin-contract evidence are attached.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior current-main session, outbound, Gateway, and security work makes this the strongest available owner for the product-boundary decision.
